utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the Prosecution continues, the Trial Chamber would like to make a statement on the proceedings. The Trial Chamber held proceedings in closed session on the 15th and 27th of May. As a result of these proceedings and the submissions made, the Trial Chamber has decided to separate the trial of the accused Milan Simic from the other three accused - Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric - in order to protect the interests of justice, as provided under Rule 82 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Consequently, the Prosecution is ordered to file an amended indictment against the three accused - Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. The Prosecution can go ahead with continued examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one quick question relating to the amended indictment. Must it be filed by a certain date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, right away, forthwith, as soon as you can file it, the better.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when we left off we were discussing a meeting that occurred in Bosanski Samac for military reserve officers in December of 1991. What we're going to do now is continue on chronologically, and we're going to move to January of 1992. In January of 1992, did you still oversee an independent military unit, the purpose of which was to protect Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did oversee it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you explained yesterday how you were able to obtain some 50 rifles but very little ammunition; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to do at this time is discuss some other substances of armaments that you received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown document D4/4, please. 4/4 and 4/4 ter, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you look at that document, please.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it would be fair for the Defence to put the B/C/S version on the ELMO, because the accused cannot understand the English version, which is now on the ELMO. If it could be placed on the ELMO for just one moment so that they can see the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Sometimes because the witness also has to look at the B/C/S version, perhaps we allow just a few minutes for the witness to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's such a short document. It's self-explanatory. You can just leave the B/C/S document on there. No problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we can have it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us what that document represents?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a receipt indicating that on the 10th of January, 1992, I gave 20 kilogrammes of Vitezit 20 explosive and 12 metres of slow-burning fuse to Nerfid Dzananovic. My signature is on the left-hand side and on the right-hand side is the signature of Mr. Nerfid Dzananovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And this gentleman that you gave the 20 kilogrammes of explosive to, where was he from and what did he do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from Odzak, and he had a function in the Territorial Defence of the Odzak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you obtained that receipt, what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That receipt, why did you get a written receipt for that document, first?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave this receipt to Mr. Djananovic. I gave him -- I issued him the explosive, to Mr. Djananovic, so I wrote the receipt. I didn't get the receipt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why did you put together a receipt? Was that part of your proper military procedures, to get a receipt?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did that in order to verify which quantity of explosives was issued to whom; in other words, the explosives were under control, and it wasn't possible for everybody to have access to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what did you do with that receipt after you signed it and this gentleman from the other TO signed it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put it in my briefcase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you eventually take it home?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I kept it at home because I did not have an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was that later seized, that document? Was it seized from your home or from the TO?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When my apartment was looted, this document was found in my briefcase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, with a pointer, could you please point to your signature, and also point to the signature of the other gentleman from the TO in Prud.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature and this is the signature of the gentleman from Odzak, to whom I gave the 20 kilogrammes of explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And above the signatures, all that language above the signatures, who wrote that out?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the words written here, "receipt" and the sentence written here: "issued," received by this name here, I wrote that. This here is my signature and this is the signature of Mr. Nerfid Djananovic, and this is the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, on that original, there are two names on the bottom. As you're facing it, the bottom right-hand corner Fitozovic A, Atic Ratif. Did you write those names?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you completed that receipt, were those names, those two names, on that receipt?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who put those names on that receipt, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would the Bench like to compare the handwriting? Because if you look at it closely, you can see that -- just on the screen you can see the letter "A," up in the top part of it, is pointed, kind of like a triangle, however, the letter A on the bottom is like an H. The rest of the printing is all capital letters. It's small and capital, but if the Court would like to examine that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as a matter of principle, I do object, because neither this Honourable Trial Chamber nor the parties here are experts in handwriting, so it's more a principle objection. If the Prosecution wants to establish certain relationship between these two handwritings, then they should contact the expert on that field and then file the expert opinion. I mean, speaking of the standards of the criminal proceedings, that's all that is the basis of my objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. The objection is sustained. We can look at the original. This is a document we've seen before?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's already in evidence. But all I'm just trying to say is since the witness has indicated it's not his, it wasn't on the document when he signed the receipt. Apparently it was placed on there sometime after, and I just wanted the Court to look at it and make not an expert opinion, but just a general opinion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can look at it. One way you can deal with the matter is to follow the course of custody of this document, because the witness has said after signing all this and writing all this he put it in his briefcase. From there, what happened to the document? That's one line of looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, on April 17th, was your house searched?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: By whom was your house searched on April 17th?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house was searched by the Grey Wolves and by the security officers in the Samac municipality, and they were under control of the 17th Tactical Group. In fact, these were the security officers from the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How do you know that security officers from the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA was involved in a search of your home?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received that information from my wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the usher can show us the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And just once again, during the search of your house, that and documents from your briefcase were taken?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's continue. You gave 20 kilogrammes of explosive to this gentleman from the TO in Prud. Where did you get the explosive?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, again just -- I believe that my dear colleague overlooked something. It is the second time that he put to the witness that it is a gentleman from Prud, and actually he was from Odzak, and that's what the witness stated. So just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That's my fault, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: From the -- the individual from TO in Odzak, you indicated you gave is this 20 kilogrammes of explosive. Did you -- let's try another question. Did you obtain a certain quantity of explosive in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How much explosive did you obtain in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hundred kilos.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When in 1991 did you obtain that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in mid-October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, where were you storing it? In an office? Without giving the specific location. In an office, in a home, in a building of some kind? Where was it being stored?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day when I got it, I stored it in my parents' house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And from there, what did you do with it? Without stating the exact location, was it placed in an office, in a factory, in a home? What did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I moved the explosive. I gave it to one of our members for storage. We're now talking about 80 kilos of explosive out of the total quantity, the 20 kilos that I gave to Mr. Djananovic was missing. Yes, of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, of that remaining 80, did you use any of that explosive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The explosive was never used. It was hidden in a septic tank. It was dry. It was no longer in use. And there it was safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why did you obtain that large quantity of explosive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, every military needs explosives, not only for sabotage work, but also for other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The witness exactly said: Every army needs explosive." I kindly ask this correction in transcript, page 8, and the line 16. Because this word, I think it's not a proper translation what the witness said. He said: "Every army needs explosive."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll leave that to the interpreters, Mr. Pantelic, because they did get the answer, and they've given us the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would prefer clarification with the learned friends from the Translation Unit immediately, if we can do that. Otherwise I have to obtain the audiotape, then make a written submission, and try to correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Weiner can get clarification from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we need some clarification for the transcript. Did you say "Everybody army needs explosive" or, "Every military or military unit needs explosives"?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every military unit needs to have explosive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that every military unit needs it. Were there other military units in Bosanski Samac that had explosives?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were other units that had explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What other units, if you know, in Bosanski Samac had explosives?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army had it, and all the four detachments that surrounded Bosanski Samac had the explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how were you able to state that? What's your basis of knowledge as to that fact, sir, as to those facts?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw the explosives when the members of the 4th Detachment drove it, when the bridge on the River Bosna was blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Let's move on to February of 1992. Within your unit, were patrols still being utilised?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were patrols that carried out the same type of activity that they did in the previous months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. I wonder whether you could seek a clarification, page 9, line 20, where the witness says: "I personally saw the explosive when the members of the 4th Detachment drove it." Drove it where? Drove it where, of course, is my question at the end of the quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, Judge Williams just had a question for you, and as you heard it, she wanted to know more information about what exactly you saw in relation to this explosive being transported. Could you give us some background, some dates, and tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw when the explosive was transported on a blue truck that belonged to the agricultural company in Bosanski Samac. It was a blue truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what date was this that you saw the explosive being transported on a blue truck?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th of April - I know for sure that that is the date - and I also saw it quite some time before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you saw it being transported on a blue truck on the 25th of April, did something happen in Bosanski Samac on or about that same date?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The explosive was transported in the afternoon, and I saw the truck as it turned left towards the bridge on the River Bosna. Around 9.00 p.m. there was an explosion, and the bridge was partially blown up. They didn't do it properly. So again, at midnight on the same date, another loud explosion was heard and the bridge was blown up completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, how did you know that members of the 4th Detachment were transporting this quantity of explosive, or some quantity of explosive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I saw them. From the position where I was, I was able to see all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you able to recognise some of the people involved in the transportation of the explosives?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did recognise some.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Any further questions, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I didn't, but now you've prompted one, I'll make one. The witness says: "Yes, I did recognise some." Are we going on to hear who the "some" are?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was going to do it at a later time, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any of those individuals who you saw transporting the explosive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw members of the 4th Detachment. I can say for sure that Fadil Topcagic was there too, and Cviko Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Fadil Topcagic, who you saw with the explosives or with the truck with the explosives, is he related to any of the defendants in this case?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is related to Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to February 1992. Were you still using -- you indicated you were still using patrols. Were these both daytime and evening patrols?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were both daytime and night-time patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And these patrols were strictly being used to make observations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I already said, they were only making observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sometime in late February or possibly even March, was there an incident that occurred in relation to one of these patrols at the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please tell the Court what exactly happened.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At night, around midnight, on our checkpoint there were three of our men in a special car. They were sitting in the car, in the passenger car, and a JNA vehicle came from the direction of Crkvina. This vehicle was -- is known as pinzgauer. Soldiers got out of this vehicle and surrounded the passenger vehicle that our patrol was in. They disarmed them and then they left for Crkvina, which is the same direction that they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me just --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This patrol notified me of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just stop you there. You indicated first they were in a special car. Was this car marked in any manner?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. The colour, the way it looked, the type of car, was just like a JNA car. Other units did not have these vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. First I was talking about the car that the three men were in, the three men who were members of your unit. Were they in a private vehicle or were they in some sort of military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in a private vehicle. This vehicle did not have any marks belonging to any unit. It was just a regular passenger private vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you said the JNA troops came by in something known as a pinzgauer. What is a pinzgauer? Is that a truck or is it a car or ... Please tell the Court what it is.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a typical military vehicle, and it is used for transporting the troops, the people, armed personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you learned of this incident, did you respond in some manner?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tell the Court what you did.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This morning, the entrances into the town from the direction of Crkvina were closed, and also the entrance from the direction of east, so the eastern entrance into the town was blocked as well and also the southern entrance into the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you use to block these entrances?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In both situations, we used buses and one vehicle belonging to the public transportation system. There were also some personal vehicles that were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What happened in the morning hours, when these roadways, these two roadways, were blocked?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On these roadblocks were our men, and they were not armed. They had no uniforms on because we didn't have any uniforms. They also did not wear any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What effect did this have on the morning traffic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that morning, no car could enter the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone contact you after these roadblocks were established?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Tihic contacted me, Sulejman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you have some conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we talked, and I explained to him what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, Tihic and Izetbegovic went to Pelagicevo, and they talked to second colonel -- lieutenant colonel or colonel - I'm not sure. I think he was a lieutenant colonel at the time. His name was Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As a result of Izet Izetbegovic's and Sulejman Tihic's conversation with Colonel Nikolic, did you receive any further telephone calls?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Tihic called me and he said to me that I should remove these roadblocks, and he told me that these three rifles that had been taken away from us will be returned. However, at that moment I didn't agree to this, and I asked for some additional conditions to be met.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did you request?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I requested the 4th Detachment to be completely disarmed. I asked for the arms that we had to also be put under a certain kind of control, because before that there had been uncontrolled shooting around the town by the 4th Detachment members. They were scaring the citizens of Bosanski Samac. They were shooting in different parts of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What happens next?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, Tihic told me that a meeting would be held in Bosanski Samac, and he asked me to remove these roadblocks nevertheless. And he said we would talk in the afternoon to the representatives of the military, the representative of the 4th Detachment, and other political structures in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were the roadblocks removed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime around noon these roadblocks were removed and the situation normalised.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long were those roadblocks erected or present at those two locations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About nine or ten hours. That's how it took altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were roadblocks ever erected again by persons under your control or with your involvement?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After that we did not make any more roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't make any more roadblocks. Did the JNA continue to have its own roadblocks at different locations in the city?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA had its checkpoints. Those were not typical roadblocks. You couldn't pass unless you had shown your ID and unless they found out what your religion and ethnicity was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So did the JNA and the local Serbs continue to utilize those checkpoints, stopping all persons who entered the city?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they continued with all their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to March of 1992, and at this time let's focus a bit on the defendants. You indicated that you had known Blagoje Simic for many years. Did you know him prior to his becoming involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had known him for many years, before he became involved in politics as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you notice any change in him after he had become involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I noticed certain changes in the mentioned gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please explain to the Court the changes that you noticed in the defendant Blagoje Simic after he became involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Blagoje Simic as a very nice gentleman. He was a medical doctor. I used to be his patient. I never thought that he would go into politics in such a way. As a matter of fact, I was surprised when, publicly and through the media, I listened to his political speeches. It wasn't a pleasant surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What was he saying that wasn't -- that you didn't find pleasant?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the very fact that he advocated the creation of a Serbian municipality of Samac and the borders that were mentioned and the fact that the municipality should be divided between the Croatian and the Serbian part. Of course, neither Muslims nor Croats agreed with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did he make any other statements after being involved in politics relating to Greater Serbia or anything in relation to Serbian nationalism?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me say the following: I wasn't very interested in Blagoje Simic's political work. He was a politician. I had other things to do. I was getting ready for the war. So I knew what he was trying to achieve, but that's all I was interested in. I was interested in other things. I was worried about certain things that were happening. Some other politicians could maybe say more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You indicated you knew that he was -- what he was trying to achieve. What was he trying to achieve, based on what you had heard?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wanted to see the creation of a Serbian municipality of Samac, of a Serbian police. The Serbian military already existed. I think this was a project of a Greater Serbia, but as I said, I think others can testify more about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you knew Miroslav Tadic for many years. Was Miroslav Tadic the owner of a certain business?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I had known Miroslav Tadic for about 30-some years. He was the owner of a cafe called AS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us: In the winter and spring of 1992 how the Cafe AS was being used?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than its regular activities, this cafe also provided a safe haven for the members of the 4th Detachment. This is where they gathered. If they had something -- if they had to collect some money their duties that they did, that's what they would do, and so, in other words, other than regular patrons, the members of the 4th Detachment also gathered at this cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did military individuals other than those in the 4th Detachment also visit the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those that were around the town, those that were located around the town, members of those units would also come to this cafe from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say "members of those units," are you referring to members of the JNA army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to JNA members, and I'm also referring to the Chetnik unit, the Grey Wolves. They would also come to the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How do you know Serbian paramilitaries known as the Grey Wolves were visiting Miroslav Tadic's Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I had said, we had these patrols around the town, and they were monitoring what was going on, and naturally, the Cafe AS was also monitored. We would monitor who was coming in and coming out of it, so that the people that were in the patrols monitoring the town noticed these men, and also the very members of the 4th Detachment would give me their reports, and they confirmed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You indicated that it was a safe haven. Was the location of the Cafe AS significant in relation to why it was being used?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I were to choose a cafe, if I belonged to that side, I would have chosen that same place. It is outside of the very town centre, and it was in an area populated more by Serbs. There was Novo Naselje there, then Pisari, then Skaric, and so on. So I think this was a well-chosen location for something like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I wonder whether you could clarify. You mentioned, page 18, line 6, this is a quotation: "Also, the very members of the 4th Detachment would give me their reports, and they confirmed this." I wonder whether you could clarify who these very members of the 4th Detachment who reported to you and confirmed that Cafe AS was being used in the manner you describe were, if you could tell us who these persons were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 4th Detachment, as I have said before, I described the way it was created. It was created by two political parties that existed in Bosanski Samac. Those two were SDP and Movement for Yugoslavia. And technically speaking, it had the support of the JNA, and it also had the material support of the JNA. And anybody, whoever wanted to, could join it. So people belonging to my ethnic group also joined the 4th Detachment, and also some people that I sent and asked to become members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And perhaps you could give some examples of who these persons were who reported back to you, who these "very members," in your words, of the 4th Detachment were who reported back to you on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be a little bit clearer, I'll say the following: Those were the people that belonged to the unit that I created, but their job was also to join the 4th Detachment so that we could know what was going on at the 4th Detachment. All the information was transmitted in such a way, directly from the 4th Detachment I would get information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, maybe Mr. Weiner could clarify for you. I was asking who, not the general, but the specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we're going to do that, number one, I don't know if he's going to be willing to turn over the name of his informers, but I think we should probably go to closed session. I don't know if these people are still living there, living in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. Weiner. We'll leave that line of questioning for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Without naming any names, sir, one question: How many of these persons did you have that infiltrated the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at the beginning that there were two men, and then, as time went by, as the aggression against Bosanski Samac was getting closer, this number increased to about ten, and they had a very specific job to do within the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, were you able to learn, in March or April, who, at least on paper, was the commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 4th Detachment was Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Based on what you had seen, as well as what you were learning from your infiltrators, who did you learn was in reality the commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Simo Zaric, although I would like to add something more: Other than this position that he held here, he also had distinct duties inside the command of the 17th Tactical Group. I think that was his main duty. Here, on the other hand, he used his influence, his reputation. This person that I already mentioned, Radovan Antic, didn't have any of that, but Simo Zaric did. But it cannot be disputed that he was the commander of the 4th Detachment, of the morale part of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, who did you learn was coordinating all the day-to-day operations and activities of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Zaric. I had an opportunity to talk to him about the situation a number of times, about the situation in the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who from the 4th Detachment was working and meeting with Colonel Nikolic and the JNA leaders?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to continue on in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit 6/4 and 6/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, it might be easier if you could try and read it right off the machine as opposed to the computer.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it like this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a document about issuing certain things, items, and the name is Ratif Atic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is that a receipt for ammunition, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a receipt. It is a document confirming issuance of certain items. This means that Ratif Atic was issued these items that are mentioned on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you read exactly what he received?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Long Luger 9 millimetres. This is a bullet, 5.000 pieces. Number 2, 7.62, armoured person [As interpreted] bullets, 2.520 pieces. And then the next one is armour person bullets -- ordinary bullets, 1260 is the number of items. Number 4 is ammunition in clip, and number 5 is a ROB, ten pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The majority of bullets are Luger-type bullets. What are those for?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're used for the automatic weapons that we discussed, the 30 pieces of automatic weapons. The 5.000 pieces referred to precisely the ammunition for that type of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So those were 5.000 bullets or shells for those old World War II rifles, those old World War II German rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the remaining bullets, were those for the other rifles that you had obtained?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The ammunition listed under 2 and 3 and 4, this is the ammunition for the weapons that we had obtained, I mean the 20 automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what about the ammunition listed under 5?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the hand grenade, the defensive hand grenade, M-75. It's used for defensive purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that receipt is dated March 2nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 2nd of March. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like you to continue on, and let's discuss another incident which occurred late in March, possibly early in April, and it was a shooting involving individuals by the name of Danilo and Tota. Do you recall the incident that I'm mentioning?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court, as best you can recall, what had happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, at around 1600 hours, Osman Mesic came to my apartment. He came in his car, which was a Golf. He was quite upset. He told me that we had to get away from the town because the members of the 4th Detachment wanted to kill us that very evening, at 11.00 p.m. precisely. And he suggested that we flee towards Rijeka, which is in the Republic of Croatia. I calmed him down and I told him that such stories were going around over the past four or five months and that it was not a big deal because that was how the psychological operations were conducted, psychological warfare. He did not listen to me, and he went to Rijeka, so I didn't manage to convince him to stay. He went to Rijeka. That day I had some meetings, and at around 10.30 I went to a cafe called Molla. And at 11.00, precisely, a yellow Lada car stopped in front of the cafe. There were three people inside the car. The driver was Mersad Mesic, who was a butcher in the town. Izet Ramusovic, Tota; and Danilo. I don't remember his last name. At that moment, the person sitting in the passenger seat and the person sitting behind the driver started rolling down the windows slowly, the windows on the car, and they started pointing their automatic weapons at the entrance to the Molla cafe. At that moment a shot was fired from a pistol. That shot was fired by the driver, the butcher that I just mentioned. In the meantime, in the immediate vicinity of the building there was a police patrol, I mean the reserve police, and before they opened fire on the Molla cafe, where I was - there were also some other patrons there - the reserve police officers opened fire on the yellow Lada car. The car stopped later, but as soon as the shot was fired from the pistol, they started driving, and then some 50 or 60 metres later the car stopped and all three members of the 4th Detachment were wounded. They were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of matters, sir, with regard to your story about what had occurred. You mentioned the name of Tota Ramusovic. Tota has a brother Izet, who is a plumber. Do you know Tota's first name? Was Tota's first name Izet or something else?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tota's name I think is Nizam. Izet is his brother, Izet Ramusovic. Later on he became the member of the Territorial Defence in Bosanski Samac, and I have to apologise for this mistake. Nizam Ramusovic, nicknamed Tota.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So Izet Ramusovic wasn't present at this incident?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, Tota, Mersad, and Danilo, were they members of any military organisation?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I have already said, they were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, Tota was of what ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim or a Montenegrin. I'm not sure. But I think he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that there were Muslims within the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you describe the types of people that were in the 4th Detachment, basically with regard to the Muslims? What could you -- how could you describe them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were mostly people who were not -- who were poor, of low social background, many of them were unemployed at the time, and the 4th Detachment paid its members.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were there any criminals among the Muslim members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were criminals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. I think the form of this question was not properly made, because this witness obviously cannot testify whether someone is criminal or not. Maybe the other way could be more appropriate, because it's rather a narrow issue to judge whether someone is criminal or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, yes, because counsel could ask whether he knew of them having any criminal records.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of the Muslims who were members of the 4th Detachment, were you aware that any of them possessed criminal records?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that most of them had criminal records with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were these persons that had criminal records given guns by the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were given guns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When I talked about criminal records, I was referring to a person who has been prosecuted in a criminal court and been convicted, not just somebody whom the police have questioned. So if you can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge of some of these persons, were you aware that any of these persons that you indicated were criminals had been prosecuted and convicted of crimes?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that some had served sentences in prison. They had been prosecuted before a criminal court and they went to prison. I don't know the type of criminal offences for which they were tried, but they were -- none of them was convicted of murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's good to know. Let us move to April 1992. What was the atmosphere in Bosanski Samac in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The atmosphere in April - and this is quite logical, in fact - was more complex than in the months before. The shooting all over the town continued, done by the 4th Detachment. They were diversions or sabotages on, for instance, the transmission lines leading towards the Republic of Croatia, and also on the buildings that were privately owned by Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You talked about sabotages. Could you please describe what you mean by "sabotages of privately owned buildings or homes of Muslims or Croats"? What happened in these instances?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the village of Skaric, on the boundary between the Bosanski Samac town and Skaric, a building belonging to Hasan Ceribasic was destroyed. Now, whether it was blown up or set alight, I can't tell you for sure, but at any rate, it was destroyed. Then a building owned by Begmin Adman - I can't remember the name - Kapetanovic was also destroyed. And in the immediate vicinity of my apartment, 70 metres from where my bedroom was, a stall or a kiosk owned by Mr. Grga Zubak was blown up. Then the power transmission lines were blown up in March and in April. So the sabotages followed each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, these power transmission lines that were blown up, did those affect the electrical power within Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As the result of these sabotages, the eastern part of the Republic of Croatia no longer had power. That means the Osijek, Vukovar, Vinkovci area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at that time was the Republic of Croatia involved in a war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, war was going on in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Between the Republic of Croatia and whom?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the Republic of Croatia and Yugoslavia, or the Yugoslav People's Army, or the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were people tense or nervous or upset after these incidents were occurring?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, the situation was such that things were coming to a head. There were shootings, those sabotages, and then the exchanges from the Republic of Croatia took place through Bosanski Samac, and sometimes the buses would stop in Bosanski Samac, full of people who had to be exchanged in Croatia, or rather, the refugees from Vukovar were on those buses. The reason why I mentioned this is because this also led to a polarisation in the town. On the one hand, there were the Muslims and Croats, and on the other, there were Serbs. When we learned or saw that these poor people from Vukovar came to Bosanski Samac to be exchanged, we got organised and we prepared coffee, tea, hamburgers or kebabs for them. On some occasions the funds from the SDA were used to provide some assistance for these people who were on their way to Croatia, to feed them, and this caused problems in the town. Even the humanitarian acts that we did bothered somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, these people who run these buses that were brought from Vukovar, Croatia, into Bosanski Samac, of what ethnic group did they belong?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were ethnic Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, during the end of the first week of April 1992, did the Bosnia-Herzegovinian presidency issue a decision?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The presidency and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued a decision about the -- in fact, they issued an order on the establishment of the municipal staffs of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what that order was?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was issued in the written form. I don't know if I understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. Could you just summarise what the order was about? Tell the Court, please, as best you can.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order stated that the presidency and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and so on and so forth, issued an order on the establishment of the municipal staffs of the Territorial Defence, in light of the fact that the staffs of the Territorial Defence that had existed until that date did not function, or in the municipalities where they existed, or where Serbs in fact lived. They engaged in certain activities for the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, as a result of this order, did it have any affect on the happenings in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did have an effect. It was a two-fold effect. When the order came, the order on the establishment of the reorganised TO municipal staffs, the residents of the Bosanski Samac municipality received this very gladly, and they thought that this whole thing would end and that all the weapons, the huge amounts of weapons that existed in the town, would end up under the control of a single entity. On the other hand, when this order came in, the situation in the town became even more complex. The shootings occurred again, the provocations by the members of the 4th Detachment occurred again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, was a meeting held in response to this order from the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after the notification of this order was received, the multiparty talks were held in the municipality. Of course, the SDS refused to accept this. The other two leading parties accepted the establishment of the Territorial Defence, and on the basis of these talks and agreements that had been reached, it was proposed that the commander of the newly established Territorial Defence would be Marko Bozanovic, and the chief of staff of the Territorial Defence -- I was supposed to be the chief of staff. I think that the proposal was dispatched to Sarajevo on that very same day, and I was appointed to the post of the Chief of Staff of the TO of the Bosanski Samac municipality on the 10th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, even prior to that, sometime after the order came down from the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you start doing something as a result of that order?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the situation was getting more and more complex, as I have already said, there were rumours in the town that the Territorial Defence would be established and people started getting interested in that: Muslims, Croats, and Serbs alike. And in this sense -- at any rate, we had an opinion poll done in the town itself, and the residents were able to put their signature, put their name and their ID number, without being forced to do so, of their own free will, so they were able to also put down what their specialty was in the former JNA. A large number of residents responded, and when they saw what was going on, they all sought weapons, but we had only the 50 rifles that we had in December, as I have already explained here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, is it time for our afternoon break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have our break and resume our proceedings at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Fitozovic. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You told us that you took a poll to determine the interest within Bosanski Samac of the TO. How did you do this? Did you make calls on the telephone? Did you set up a polling booth? How did you go about doing this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did the poll publicly, in the centre of the town, before the official reorganised Territorial Defence was set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was this after the decision came down from the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was before the decision of the presidency and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as after the decision of the government and the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina about the setting up of the new Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And there was a great deal of interest in the re-establishment of the Territorial Defence, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated at some point Marko Bozanovic was nominated as commander and you were nominated as chief of staff, and your names were sent along to Sarajevo. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you pay a visit to the Territorial Defence building in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I paid a visit to the Territorial Defence building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On what date?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 13th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was the condition of the interior: The desks, records?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the offices in the building were concerned, everything was empty. The desks were empty, the shelves were empty. And the warehouse had been emptied of weapons before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about records of the persons who had performed military service in the community? What happened to the records?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the staff of the Territorial Defence itself, we did not find any documentation that would say anything about the organisation of the former TO or of the names of the members of the TO or the reserve of the TO. It's important to emphasise that these same records, that is to say, the entire military documentation, was taken by the JNA. This entire military documentation that was at the Secretariat for National Defence had been taken to Brcko before by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was planning to show him three photographs. I know you -- both Judges here are quite familiar with the photographs, but I thought it might be helpful to Judge Lindholm when he gets back and reviews the video to see three different photographs from different angles of the TO and its relation to the SUP or police department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I see from Exhibit 14A photographs 50, 2, and 4, please. Photograph 50, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, that is photograph 50 from Prosecutor's Exhibit 14A. Do you recognise the building in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Territorial Defence building, the building of the staff of the Territorial Defence; and this in the background is the warehouse of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is there a courtyard in the middle, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is where the yard is, here, behind this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, the witness has pointed to a building directly in front of the picture, or directly -- slightly to the right of the picture, which is behind a white car and a black car, and he's indicated that that is the TO building; that the yard to the left is the courtyard and the building behind is the warehousing buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at photograph 2. Do you recognise the buildings and area depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the building of the SUP, the police, of the Bosanski Samac municipality, and it was taken from the courtyard of the Territorial Defence courtyard -- Territorial Defence staff building. So this is the courtyard of the TO building. This is where the warehouse is and this is part of the main building. And this was the garage, in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, photograph 2 depicts the courtyard of the Territorial Defence, and directly across from the Territorial Defence and the courtyard is the SUP, or the police department of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you finally show the witness photograph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the buildings depicted in photograph 4?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a photograph that was also taken from the courtyard. This is the main building, from the back. These are the auxiliary rooms. It's true that they have been run down somewhat, but this also belonged to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, in photograph 2, it depicts the courtyard. The building, if you're facing the photograph, to the right is the Territorial Defence, and the building straight ahead, he indicated, is an auxiliary building of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, with Marko Bozanovic did you begin to reorganise the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We immediately started to reorganise the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as part of that, did you try to recruit new members?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we started recruiting new members, when we entered the building of the TO, we convened all the members of the former staff of the TO, and we held a meeting with them. And the subject of the meeting was whether they wanted to continue being members of the Territorial Defence, of the new Territorial Defence. Since the former staff of the Territorial Defence was mostly formed from Serbs, two Muslims, and maybe two or three Croats, not everybody agreed to become members of the Territorial Defence. That is to say, not everybody agreed to become members of the TO staff, of the leadership of the TO, if that's clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as part of attracting people to the Territorial Defence, did you use the radio? Did you appear on any radio programmes?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 13th of April, 1992, I had an interview on the local radio station of Bosanski Samac, and there I informed the population of Bosanski Samac that a new Territorial Defence had been created, and I asked them to become members, that is to say, to register with the new Territorial Defence. We weren't doing this on the streets any more. We were doing it in Room 1, which you could see on the first photograph that we had just looked at. You could see that very office on that photograph. And on the very first day, the turnout was quite large.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, based on this turnout or these enlistments, and also considering your extensive military background, did you develop any sort of organisational plan, including certain units and the personnel that you wanted in each of these units? Did you develop any sort of plan for this Territorial Defence that you were putting together?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I made a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you explain what you did? And then I'll show you some exhibits which I believe relate to that plan.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the previous survey that we had done publicly in the town, of those members that registered voluntarily, who wanted to join the TO, of their names and their specialty that they had from the JNA, the former JNA, I made a framework how certain units within the new Territorial Defence could look.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could I see Exhibit D22/2, 16 and 17/1. For ID, yes. We can do one at a time. If you can get 16 and 17/1. Mr. Usher, we can do one at a time. We have a number that we have to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, in front of you is Exhibit D22/2 ID. Would you look at it, please, and tell me if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 4th, or Medical Squad, and it says here who the commander is, and then below are the members of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who drafted this unit plan?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan was drafted by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why did you put those particular people into that planned unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is important to mention the following, but I will first answer. I put these people in this unit because they were connected with their profession to these duties. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to mention is the following: When I was making this list, based on the survey, the members of this squad at that time didn't know that they had been given these duties. They knew that they belonged to the Territorial Defence, but they didn't know at that time what duties they would be assigned within the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just want to stop him for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is under seal, so I just want to notify the audiovisual not to display it on the screen. I think the Defence -- the defendants have had enough time to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please continue? I'm sorry for interrupting you. So basically, you were indicating that you were just putting these plans together and you had never had the opportunity to tell any of these people that they had been selected and placed in this unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. These lists were created two days before the aggression, so that I had no opportunity to gather this squad or any other unit. And that is very important to know because of the people that were on these lists, that they themselves, and I repeat, they themselves, did not know what their duties would be inside the new Territorial Defence. We were just beginning to work on the plans. We were interrupted by the aggression, so that we could not complete these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, the document in front of you, is it a fair and accurate representation of the document which you prepared back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it resembles that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And have any changes been made, omissions, deletions, changes to that document, other than the work which you had done?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, only the highlight and the number 7 has been circled. I did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what happened to this document? What did you do once you completed it? Or what happened with this draft? Did you bring it home? Did you bring it to the TO, the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put this in my briefcase because this Territorial Defence had not been consolidated yet. As I said, everything was empty. Some people were taking items out. Somebody was taking out a radio, somebody was taking out a plant pot, and I didn't dare leave this document in the Territorial Defence, because there were some other people hovering around, some other people that did not want to join the new Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what happened to those documents in your briefcase on April 17th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was found while my apartment was looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to move this as an exhibit, move it into evidence at this time. It can remain under seal, but all of the other similar type documents have been admitted, and I'd ask that this one be admitted too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I would like to hear from the Defence. There's no objection, I take it? All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On behalf of all Defence team, we don't have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I just request the Prosecution to reconfirm with me which exact document you are...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Both 22/2 and 22 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I and 22/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So this will go in the Prosecution Exhibit, even though it was submitted by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's the Prosecution who are moving it to be an exhibit, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be P65/ter and P65, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And just one question. The statement across the top, stating what type of list that is, is that "Medical Unit"? Is that what it says across the top of that document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Medical Squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you look at the next document, please, 17/1 and 17/1 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, we're just trying to find out. This is the document which was under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Do you still want -- the one which you've just moved as an exhibit, do you still want it under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. It was under seal at the time because it related to a protected witness, and they highlighted the name of a relative of a protected witness and they also circled the number in relation to that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it could remain under seal. I have ... If there's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we keep it under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to prevent any confusion, if this is the document D22/2, that is the document that has already been marked on the 14th of February it was presented by my colleague Mr. Zecevic during the examination of Witness G, and at that time the document was already marked, and it no longer had the identification mark. So I don't think that it's necessary for the document to get any other number, because if this is the document we're talking about, it was described as "the medical corps document."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We still have it listed as an ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I can see -- because we received the update on exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may help, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Documents D22A down to D22/I were admitted on the 19th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. So they are already exhibits as Defence exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And they are all under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. So we have to retract the number which was announced as P65. Yes. So they will retain the original number. Yes, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you look at that next document, sir, and could you read the title along the top, please.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's, "Hunters' Squad."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who prepared that document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drafted this document, although some numbers here are not printed in the proper manner, which is not the way that I would do it, but the names correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, how did you select people for this squad?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Hunters' Squad was made up of licensed hunters who were registered with the municipal hunters' association. The men listed here on this list, under 1 through 9, and also the persons listed under 1 and 2, and the commander, signed the document, indicating that they voluntarily joined the Territorial Defence of the Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say that they signed the document, you're not referring to this particular document, this Hunters' Squad document. Are you talking about the document that you signed if you were interested in joining the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely the document I'm talking about. And I just wanted to note here that the members of the Territorial Defence listed here did not know, because there was no time to learn, that they were members of this squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And approximately what date was this list prepared?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I prepared it on the 14th or 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Could you look at the next exhibit, 16/1?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And place 16/1 ter on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And while we're looking at this, could we also get two more ready: 8/2 and 24/2. Thank you. Now, what is the title on the top of this document? We're referring to 16/1 and 16/1 ter. Could you please read the title out.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Communications Squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who selected the people for this squad?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I selected these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who drafted this list of people in the Communication Squad, or the Communication Section, that's depicted on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, approximately when was this list drafted?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the lists were made in a single day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And this list here, is this similar to the others, where the persons assigned to this squad were never notified of this assignment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. For instance, in the Communications Squad, the commander -- may I read out his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure. No problem.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the squad was Safet Hadzialijagic. He didn't know that he was the commander of the squad, and neither did the others listed here, listed under 1 through 9. Perhaps some of them did know, because there was the electronic communications, the courier communications, all kinds of communications, and these people were selected on the basis of the lists where people reported voluntarily to join the Territorial Defence of the Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Let's go on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the registry just confirm this next one, 8/2 and 8/2 ter is an ID, it's not an exhibit at this time? That's what our records indicate here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. Weiner. It's still a document, not an exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you read the title of this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title of this document -- first of all, this is attachment number 4.2, copy number -- it's entitled the Anti-Sabotage Squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What was an anti-sabotage squad?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan was for this squad to be part of the Territorial Defence of a unit formed by the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you select the persons that were placed on this list?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did select the persons on this list, but here, person under 5 it says here "arrested," and I didn't arrest anyone. I don't know what happened to number 7, because I can't see it, whether he was killed or arrested. I can't really read it. But I couldn't put the words "arrested" or "killed" on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The list -- or first: You drafted this particular list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you typed it up, or did you have someone type it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite certain that I did not type up this list. Perhaps somebody else did it for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the words that you did not include there, the "arrested" and then across from number 7 some other words, those aren't typewritten; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. They're not typed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how did you determine who was going to be on that list, on the Anti-Sabotage Squad or Unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I decided to include the persons who had undergone training in the former Yugoslav People's Army for such operations. In some cases I went a bit further and I included those who were a bit braver than others, those who were not scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
